title: Cap. IX Arg. 8 Sol cont.: they wrongly slide from reprobation to damnation — two things hanging on diverse causes
latin: Ultimo, perperam in hoc argumento transcursunt a reprobatione ad ipsam damnationem, et haec duo inter se commiscere et confundere conantur, quae ex diversis causis pendere supra ostendimus. Neque tamen damus illis, posita hac hypothesi (quae Catholicae Ecclesiae judicio semper fuit approbata) Damnari nonnullos propter solum originale peccatum, inde consequi Deum rigidius agere cum talibus, quam cum ipsis diabolis. Non enim dicimus judicem rigidius agere cum minore reo quovis, quam cum deterrimo proditore, quod utrumque damnet, nisi eum, qui minore peccato tenetur, pari aut majori supplicio afficiat.
pass_a: Lastly, wrongly in this argument they run across from reprobation unto damnation itself, and endeavor to mingle and confound these two between themselves, which we have above shown to hang from diverse causes. Nor yet do we grant them that, this hypothesis being posited (which by the judgment of the Catholic Church has always been approved) That some are damned on account of original sin alone, it thence follows that God deals more rigidly with such than with the very demons. For we do not say that a judge deals more rigidly with any lesser guilty one than with the worst traitor, because he damns both, unless he afflict him who is held by a lesser sin with equal or greater punishment.
pass_b: Lastly: in this argument they wrongly slide from reprobation to damnation itself, and try to mix and confuse the two — which we have already shown hang on diverse causes. Nor do we grant that, on the hypothesis always approved by the Catholic Church's judgment — that some are damned for original sin alone — it follows God deals more rigidly with such than with the very demons. A judge is not said to deal more rigidly with a lesser offender than with the worst traitor merely because he condemns both, unless he afflicts the one held by the lesser crime with equal or greater punishment.

lemmas.gloss: must not confuse reprobation with damnation
same sentence ≠ greater rigor unless penalty heavier

title: Cap. IX Arg. 8 Sol cont.: Augustine — infants go into the mildest of all damnation, demons into the bitterest; degrees in eternal damnation unknown
latin: Jam vero, utcunque Deus damnet parvulos solo originali peccato contaminatos et constrictos, ac damnet etiam diabolos actualis et nefariae rebellionis reos, tamen in modo et gradu poenae inflictiae ingens discrimen est. Nam infantes (ut bene Augustinus, De peccat. mer. et remiss. l. 1. cap. 16.) exeunt in damnatione omnium mitissima; daemones in damnatione longe acerbissima. Nulla autem acies ingenii humani potest discernere, quot possunt esse gradus poenarum in eadem damnatione aeterna: ac proinde inconsequens est haec argumentatio, Parvuli damnantur ob peccatum originale, et Diaboli tantum damnantur ob peccatum actuale, Ergo parvuli rigidius tractantur.
pass_a: Now truly, howsoever God damns little ones contaminated and bound by original sin alone, and also damns the demons guilty of actual and nefarious rebellion, yet in the mode and degree of the punishment inflicted there is a huge difference. For infants (as Augustine well, De peccat. mer. et remiss. l. 1. cap. 16.) go forth into the mildest of all damnation; the demons into damnation by far the bitterest. But no edge of human wit can discern how many degrees of punishments there can be in the same eternal damnation: and therefore this argumentation is inconsequent, Little ones are damned on account of original sin, and the Devils are damned only on account of actual sin, Therefore little ones are more rigidly treated.
pass_b: However God damns infants stained and bound by original sin alone, and also damns demons guilty of actual wicked rebellion, there is a huge difference in the mode and degree of the punishment inflicted. Infants (as Augustine well says, De peccat. mer. et remiss. 1.16) go into the mildest of all damnation; demons into damnation far the bitterest. No edge of human wit can tell how many degrees of pains there may be in the same eternal damnation. So this argument does not follow: Infants are damned for original sin, and Devils only for actual sin; therefore infants are treated more rigidly.

lemmas.gloss: unknown degrees in eternal damnation block the rigor inference

title: Cap. IX Arg. 9: if creation of each is continuation of first creation, absolute reprobation not from foresight of final unbelief fights creation diametrically — creation would become a medium subordinated to damnation
latin: Si creatio accipiatur pro illa singularium creatione qua unusquisque suum esse a Deo accipit, quae est primae creationis quasi continuatio, tum qui reprobationem ponunt haud factam ex praevisione finalis infidelitatis, faciunt illam ex diametro pugnare cum creatione. Nam creatio sua natura est communicatio boni secundum naturalem Dei bonitatem: At cum ejusmodi statuitur esse, ut hanc habeat intentionem, quod via sit per quam reprobatio jam ante facta finem suum consequatur, non est jam communicatio boni, sed medium damnationi subordinatum. Tale autem medium statuitur ab illis, qui ponunt praedestinationem et reprobationem ex mera Dei voluntate pendere, et non ex praevisione fidei et infidelitatis.
pass_a: If creation be taken for that creation of singulars by which each one receives his being from God, which is as it were a continuation of the first creation, then they who place reprobation as by no means made from foresight of final unbelief make it fight diametrically with creation. For creation by its nature is a communication of good according to the natural goodness of God: But when it is established to be of such a sort that it has this intention, that it be a way by which reprobation already before made may attain its end, it is no longer a communication of good, but a medium subordinated unto damnation. But such a medium is established by those who place predestination and reprobation as hanging from the mere will of God, and not from foresight of faith and unbelief.
pass_b: If creation means that making of particulars by which each receives his being from God — a kind of continuation of the first creation — then those who set reprobation as not made from foresight of final unbelief make it fight creation head-on. Creation by nature is a communication of good according to God's natural goodness. But if it is cast so as to have this intention — that it be a path by which reprobation already made reaches its end — it is no longer a communication of good, but a medium subordinated to damnation. And that is the medium set by those who hang predestination and reprobation on God's mere will, not on foresight of faith and unbelief.

lemmas.gloss: creation would become means to damnation

title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol: eternal non-election no more fights temporal creation than angelic passing-over fought angelic creation — greater difficulty with angels, seen intact
latin: Negamus consequentiam Majoris. Nam aeternum Dei decretum de non-eligendis, sive reprobandis hominibus quibusdam non magis pugnare potest cum temporali eorundem creatione, quam cum Angelorum creatione pugnavit quorundam praeteritio sive non-electio, ex mera libertate voluntatis Divinae ab aeterno constituta. Imo major videtur difficultas in causa Angelorum quam hominum; Homines enim ab aeterno electi aut praeteriti repraesentabantur menti Divinae ut in massa corrupta vitiati, et reprobabiles; at Angelos integros Deus intuitus est in eadem perfectione, in qua eos postea condidit: Si igitur aeterna reprobatio quorundam Angelorum ex beneplacito Divino, et non ex peccati praevisione, orta minime pugnavit cum creatione eorundem, non potest recte concipi pugna ulla inter reprobationem et creationem hominum, qui Deo reprobanti objiciuntur, ut peccato Adae contaminati et occisi.
pass_a: We deny the consequence of the Major. For the eternal decree of God concerning certain men not to be elected, or to be reprobated, cannot fight more with their temporal creation than the passing-by or non-election of certain ones, constituted from eternity from the mere liberty of the Divine will, fought with the creation of the Angels. Nay, a greater difficulty seems in the cause of the Angels than of men; For men from eternity elected or passed by were represented unto the Divine mind as vitiated in a corrupt mass, and reprobable; but God looked upon the Angels intact in the same perfection in which he afterward founded them: If therefore the eternal reprobation of certain Angels sprung from the Divine good pleasure, and not from foresight of sin, by no means fought with their creation, no fight can rightly be conceived between the reprobation and creation of men, who are objected unto God reprobating as contaminated and slain by the sin of Adam.
pass_b: We deny the Major's consequence. God's eternal decree concerning certain men not to be elected, or to be reprobated, can no more fight their temporal creation than the passing-by or non-election of some angels — set from eternity by mere liberty of divine will — fought angelic creation. Indeed the difficulty seems greater with angels than with men. Men from eternity elect or passed by were shown to the divine mind as vitiated in a corrupt mass and reprobable; but God looked on the angels intact in the same perfection in which he later made them. So if eternal reprobation of certain angels sprung from divine good pleasure, not from foresight of sin, and in no way fought their creation, no fight can rightly be conceived between reprobation and creation of men, who are set before God reprobating as contaminated and slain by Adam's sin.

lemmas.gloss: angelic passing-over did not fight their creation
men seen corrupted; angels seen intact

title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol: Suarez and Vasquez — angels elect/non-elect with no mass of perdition; demons reprobated before any foresighted sin
latin: De Angelis habemus ipsos Jesuitas nobis assipulantes. Suares, Opuscul. De concursu Dei, lib. 2. cap. 5. In Angelis nulla erat massa perditionis aut naturae infectae, et tamen quosdam elegit Deus, alios non elegit, quosdam destinavit in honorem, alios vero reliquit ut fierent vasa contumeliae. De hominibus etiam eodem modo statuendum dicit idem Suares: Si sermo sit de non-electione, quam nonnulli reprobationem negativam vocant, sic verum est, Causam illius esse solam Dei voluntatem, nulla expectata causa ex parte hominis. Quin etiam Vasques, qui minus nobis favet in hac controversia, tamen ingenue nobis largitur, Daemones ante omne peccatum praevisum fuisse reprobatos et permissos cadere in peccatum: quam reprobationem ille vocat reprobationem a gratia, decretum non miserendi, etc., In 1. Aquinat. disp. 45. cap. 3. et 5.
pass_a: Concerning the Angels we have the Jesuits themselves assenting unto us. Suarez, Opuscul. De concursu Dei, lib. 2. cap. 5. In the Angels there was no mass of perdition or of infected nature, and yet God elected certain ones, others he did not elect, certain he destined unto honor, but others he left that they might become vessels of contumely. Concerning men also the same Suarez says it is to be established in the same manner: If the speech be concerning non-election, which some call negative reprobation, so it is true, That the cause of it is the sole will of God, no cause being awaited from the part of man. Nay even Vasquez, who favors us less in this controversy, yet frankly grants us that the Demons before every foresighted sin were reprobated and permitted to fall into sin: which reprobation he calls reprobation from grace, a decree of not pitying, etc., In 1. Aquinat. disp. 45. cap. 3. and 5.
pass_b: On the angels we have the Jesuits themselves with us. Suarez (Opusc. De concursu Dei 2.5): In the angels there was no mass of perdition or infected nature, and yet God elected some, did not elect others, destined some to honor, and left others to become vessels of contumely. Of men, the same Suarez says, it is to be held the same way: if the talk is of non-election, which some call negative reprobation, it is true that its cause is God's will alone, with no cause awaited from man's side. Even Vasquez, who favors us less in this controversy, frankly grants that the demons were reprobated and permitted to fall before any foresighted sin — which reprobation he calls reprobation from grace, a decree of not pitying, etc. (In 1. Aquin. disp. 45.3 and 5).

lemmas.gloss: angels elect/non-elect without mass of perdition

title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol: creation of Judas is not a medium subordinated to his damnation — Augustine and Prosper; to create a reprobate ≠ to create that he may be damned
latin: Potuerunt Jesuitae intelligere, quomodo creatio singulorum angelorum facta in tempore non pugnaverit cum reprobatione quorundam, sola Dei voluntate ab aeterno constituta: potuerunt idem de hominibus concipere: Intendat aciem ingenii sui Corvinus, et idem facile intelligat. Sed putat se confirmare posse consequentiam hac argumentatione: Creatio sua natura est communicatio boni: At praecesserit talis reprobatio qualem nos ponimus, erit via quaedam per quam reprobatio jam ante facta finem suum consequatur, erit medium hominis non-electi damnationi subordinatum. Ac proinde non erit communicatio boni; cum bonum aestimari debeat ex mente dantis, et fine propter quem datur. Sed haec parum solide disputantur. Nam primo creatio singularium hominum tam electionem quam reprobationem eorundem consequitur. Sicuti ergo creatio Petri improprie diceretur medium subordinatum ejus electioni, ita et creatio Judae improprie et falso dicitur medium subordinatum aut reprobationi aut damnationi ejusdem. Si qui sunt qui audeant sustinere creationem hominum esse medium damnationi eorundem subordinatum, ego ab illis dissentio, et amplector sententiam Augustini et Prosperi, qui hoc passim adversantur.
pass_a: The Jesuits were able to understand how the creation of singular angels made in time did not fight with the reprobation of certain ones, constituted from eternity by the sole will of God: they were able to conceive the same concerning men: Let Corvinus bend the edge of his wit, and he will easily understand the same. But he thinks he can confirm the consequence by this argumentation: Creation by its nature is a communication of good: But if such a reprobation as we place shall have preceded, it will be a certain way by which reprobation already before made may attain its end, it will be a medium of the non-elect man subordinated unto damnation. And therefore it will not be a communication of good; since good ought to be estimated from the mind of the giver, and from the end on account of which it is given. But these things are disputed with little solidity. For first the creation of singular men follows both their election and their reprobation. As therefore the creation of Peter would improperly be called a medium subordinated unto his election, so also the creation of Judas is improperly and falsely called a medium subordinated either unto his reprobation or unto his damnation. If there are any who dare to maintain that the creation of men is a medium subordinated unto their damnation, I dissent from them, and embrace the sentence of Augustine and Prosper, who everywhere oppose this.
pass_b: The Jesuits could see how the creation of particular angels in time did not fight the reprobation of some, set from eternity by God's will alone — and they could conceive the same of men. Let Corvinus bend his wit's edge, and he will easily see it. But he thinks he can shore up the consequence thus: Creation by nature is a communication of good; yet if such reprobation as we place preceded, it will be a path by which reprobation already made reaches its end — a medium of the non-elect man subordinated to damnation — and so will not be a communication of good, since good is to be judged from the giver's mind and the end for which it is given. That is weakly argued. First: creation of particular men follows both their election and their reprobation. As Peter's creation would improperly be called a medium subordinated to his election, so Judas's creation is improperly and falsely called a medium subordinated to his reprobation or damnation. If any dare hold that men's creation is a medium subordinated to their damnation, I dissent and embrace Augustine and Prosper, who everywhere oppose that.

lemmas.gloss: Judas's creation not subordinated to damnation
